Numbers nobody chose.

A capability, not three free functions, and for a sharper reason than the
usual one. "May read the environment" is worth seeing in a signature; "may
generate randomness" is worth seeing *and* worth pinning, because a function
that draws is a function whose test passes ninety-nine runs in a hundred.
`Random::seeded` is the whole payoff: the same seed gives the same sequence,
so a failure is reproducible and a fixture is a fixture rather than a coin
flip. `docs/design/permissions.md` draws this line — the time, the
environment and the dice are three different things to deny a dependency.

The generator is splitmix64, and it lives half here and half in the runtime:
the state is one `Int` in a `Shared`, `khora_random_step` advances it and
`khora_random_mix` turns a state into a draw. Splitting it that way is what
keeps the critical section to a single addition — see `draw` below.

**These are not cryptographic numbers.** Anyone who sees one draw can predict
every draw after it. Right for a shuffle, a retry jitter, a load-balancing
choice or a test fixture; wrong for a session token or a key, which want a
generator with a different name so that a program says which one it needed.
